description.value: The Haylmore Heritage Site commemorates Will Haylmore, the original gold claim mine recorder in the Bridge River Valley, on the property where he lived and operated near Gold Bridge. The Bridge River Valley Community Association has restored one of the buildings and a stage on the grounds, and the site now serves as both a tourism information booth and a place to purchase locally produced artisan goods. A community-owned 4 kW solar array was installed at the site in 2015 as part of a regional renewable energy initiative.

address.value: 104 Haylmore Ave, Gold Bridge BC V0K1P0

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is an active, community-operated heritage attraction and tourism information point in the remote Bridge River Valley — a legitimate and interesting stop for touring cyclists passing through Gold Bridge on routes such as the Hurley Forest Service Road.

wow_evidence: Restored property of the valley's original gold claim recorder; doubles as info booth and artisan shop — a real if modest heritage stop for Gold Bridge.
blurb: Restored property of Bridge River Valley's first gold recorder; info booth and local artisan goods.
